name: TSMC’s N7 immersion FinFET process
description: TSMC introduced its original 7 nm FinFET foundry process with 193 nm immersion lithography before selectively inserting EUV in the N7+ variant.

date.basis: Date or date granularity stated in the cited source.

events.statement: TSMC began volume manufacture on base N7.
events.caveats: N7 and N7+ are separate process variants within one foundry family.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 11, N7, N7+ and N6
evidence.supports: The annual report dates N7 volume production to April 2018.

evidence.locator: Printed pp. 3–4, C. C. Wei prepared remarks on N7 and N7+
evidence.supports: The contemporaneous call confirms volume production and identifies immersion layers replaced on the later variant.

earliest_record.rationale: The dated TSMC call and annual report establish the month of base N7 volume production.

links.statement: Base N7 extended TSMC’s use of 193 nm immersion lithography to its original 7 nm FinFET production process.
links.scope: Continuity of the 193 nm immersion method across TSMC’s process generations.
links.caveats: This establishes the lithography family. The precise inheritance of recipes, scanner models, and layers from any one preceding node remains unresolved.

evidence.supports: Identifies immersion patterning and changes to resist, masks, and scanners for 7 nm development.

evidence.locator: Printed pp. 3–4, C. C. Wei prepared remarks on N7 and N7+
evidence.supports: Confirms the base N7 production ramp and identifies immersion as the baseline for selected layers replaced by EUV in N7+.

evidence.locator: Section on TSMC and Samsung Foundry EUV adoption
evidence.supports: Separately identifies production N7 as ArF immersion, the 193 nm optical family.
